title: Asymptotic Giant Branch Stars, Mira Variables and Stellar Mass Loss Against Density and Energy Bounds

lessons.title: Lesson 1 — Settle in.
paragraphs: Welcome in. I am Professor Zofia Petrov, and this is Asymptotic Giant Branch Stars, Mira Variables and Stellar Mass Loss Against Density and Energy Bounds. This is lesson 1 of 1 in the full thirty-minute build of this class. In this lesson we take the class's own material in order — nothing here is imported, and nothing is asked later that is not taught here first. We begin here: Settle in.

Settle in. I am Professor Zofia Petrov, and this is Asymptotic Giant Branch Stars, Mira Variables and Stellar Mass Loss Against Density and Energy Bounds. This class is built on real papers — deposited, citable work. I will present each paper and what it reports; that presentation is the lesson. At the end I will ask you questions on what was taught here — nothing else.
Here is the next piece of the material, in the order the class presents it.

'Carbon Dust Budget and Wind Number Density of IRC+10216 (CW Leonis)'. Its stated result: Headline result (values verbatim from results.json): stellar_radius_Rsun = 986; mean_density_kg_m3 = 2.95e-06; pulsation_constant_Q_days = 0.0297; momentum_ratio_to_L_over_c = 1.02; kinetic_power_Lsun = 0.346; number_density_at_condensation_cm3 = 3.26e+09; shell_mass_Msun = 0.2; envelope_depletion_time_yr = 35000.
Now we go one step further into the material.

'Carbon-Star Wind Acceleration Budget and Shell Age of S Cephei'. Its stated result: Headline result (values verbatim from results.json): stellar_radius_Rsun = 645; mean_density_kg_m3 = 8.39e-06; pulsation_constant_Q_days = 0.0376; momentum_ratio_to_L_over_c = 1.39; kinetic_power_Lsun = 0.346; number_density_at_condensation_cm3 = 2.21e+09; shell_mass_Msun = 0.08; envelope_depletion_time_yr = 60000.
The next piece is where this starts to come together.

'Circumstellar Shell Budget and Envelope Density of OH 26.5+0.6'. Its stated result: Headline result (values verbatim from results.json): envelope_depletion_time_yr = 6670; shell_mass_Msun = 0.36; dust_mass_in_shell_Msun = 0.00288; number_density_at_10Rstar_cm3 = 2.55e+08; crossing_time_to_0p1pc_yr = 6520; eddington_ratio = 0.304; stellar_radius_Rsun = 1180; pulsation_cycles_in_depletion_time = 1570.
Listen carefully here — this piece carries weight in the questions later.

'Envelope Depletion Time and Dust Production Rate of R Leonis'. Its stated result: Headline result (values verbatim from results.json): stellar_radius_Rsun = 299; surface_gravity_m_s2 = 0.00308; escape_velocity_km_s = 35.8; dust_mass_loss_rate_Msun_yr = 4e-10; shell_mass_Msun = 0.0008; dust_mass_in_shell_Msun = 3.2e-06; envelope_depletion_time_yr = 3.5e+06; crossing_time_to_0p1pc_yr = 9780.
We take the pieces in order, because each one stands on the last.

'Escape Speed Comparison and Slow Wind Energetics of R Doradus'. Its stated result: Headline result (values verbatim from results.json): stellar_radius_Rsun = 358; surface_gravity_m_s2 = 0.00257; escape_velocity_km_s = 35.8; dust_mass_loss_rate_Msun_yr = 6.4e-10; shell_mass_Msun = 0.00144; dust_mass_in_shell_Msun = 5.76e-06; envelope_depletion_time_yr = 2.5e+06; crossing_time_to_0p1pc_yr = 17200.
Stay with me, because the next piece builds directly on that one.

'Long-Period Pulsation Density and Circumstellar Mass Budget of Z Puppis'. Its stated result: Headline result (values verbatim from results.json): condensation_radius_Rstar = 2; condensation_radius_AU = 5.89; number_density_at_condensation_cm3 = 3.75e+08; number_density_at_10Rstar_cm3 = 1.5e+07; number_density_at_1000AU_cm3 = 13000; mach_number_terminal = 5.64; shell_mass_Msun = 0.0165; momentum_ratio_to_L_over_c = 0.271.
Here is the next piece of the material, in the order the class presents it.

Now my worked example — this class's set problem, worked in full. The problem: Take the paper “Carbon Dust Budget and Wind Number Density of IRC+10216 (CW Leonis)”. Its stated result is: Headline result (values verbatim from results.json): stellar_radius_Rsun = 986; mean_density_kg_m3 = 2.95e-06; pulsation_constant_Q_days = 0.0297; momentum_ratio_to_L_over_c = 1.02; kinetic_power_Lsun = 0.346; number_density_at_condensation_cm3 = 3.26e+09; shell_mass_Msun = 0.2; envelope_depletion_t (a) Restate the claim in your own words. (b) Name one observation or computation that could prove it wrong. The worked answer: A strong answer restates the claim without borrowing the paper’s wording, then names a test the paper itself would accept — here, the natural test is to recompute or re-measure the headline quantity in the stated result and check it against the paper’s own number, under the paper’s own stated assumptions.

Let us gather what this lesson taught, in order: Settle in; 'Carbon Dust Budget and Wind Number Density of IRC+10216 (CW Leonis)'; 'Carbon-Star Wind Acceleration Budget and Shell Age of S Cephei'; 'Circumstellar Shell Budget and Envelope Density of OH 26.5+0.6'; 'Envelope Depletion Time and Dust Production Rate of R Leonis'; 'Escape Speed Comparison and Slow Wind Energetics of R Doradus'. Those are the pieces — hold them in that order, because the questions follow the same road.

That is the lesson, whole. Below it are the questions — every one of them drawn from what was just taught, and nothing else. The full text of this lesson stays open beside the questions, and going back to read a piece again is learning, not cheating. When you are ready, begin.
